svg.title: Merge versus rebase on the same commit graph
svg.desc: The same five-commit graph drawn twice. On the left a merge commit joins the branch back with two parents, preserving the true shape of history. On the right the branch commits are replayed as C-prime and D-prime with new hashes onto a linear history, with a red warning crossed across it about rebasing shared branches.
svg.text: Merge versus rebase on the same commit graph
C and D were REWRITTEN — new
rebase a branch others already pulled
their history diverges and the next
pull merges the same work twice
a commit is a SNAPSHOT plus parents,
not a diff. Once you believe that,
merge and rebase stop being scary:
one adds a node, the other builds
new nodes and moves the label.
has to an undo, and nobody
